html:
The Kakinte, or Caquinte, are a small people of the forested hills between the Tambo and Urubamba rivers in central Peru. They speak a language of the Kampa branch of the Arawakan family, close to those of the Asháninka and Matsigenka.

They number a few hundred and long lived in scattered households in the hills, away from the rivers, which helped them avoid much of the violence of the rubber era. Since the mid 1900s most have gathered in a few communities on the Poyeni and nearby streams.
